after_orochi_peace.text: * Orochi lowers its eight heads and sinks back into the roots, silent, the way a chained thing goes silent. The ash fades from the Waystone...
* ...and its old carvings glow again, faint and gold. A pale light comes down through the trees and hangs above the fork, calm and silent.

after_orochi_peace.speaker: Divine
after_orochi_peace.text: You showed mercy where you had every reason to show none. That is rarer than strength.

after_orochi_peace.speaker: Divine
after_orochi_peace.text: The one you hunt did not break the Overlord's sleep by force. He bargained with it. Remember that. He makes bargains.

after_orochi_peace.speaker: Divine
after_orochi_peace.text: The stone will burn again. Until the moon is new. No longer.

after_orochi_peace.speaker: Divine
after_orochi_peace.text: Your sister and brother live. He took them up the high roads. Both roads meet again in the Safaris. Ask after them in Dundean.
* For a moment the light rests on Kael's hands, warm, the way a hand rests on a child's head. Then it lifts.
* At the foot of the Waystone lies a small blue ribbon. Lira's. It is tied in a careful knot.

after_orochi_peace.speaker: Kael
after_orochi_peace.text: She left this for me. She knew I would come.

after_orochi_peace.speaker: Divine
after_orochi_peace.text: Then go. She is still on the road, and the road is long.
* Kael folds the ribbon into his coat. The light fades. Beyond the Waystone, the two high roads lie clear, and the forest lets him pass.

after_orochi_won.text: * As the last head goes down, it breathes one word: ...free...
* Then the forest is silent. The Waystone stays dark, the grey handprint still pressed into its face.
* In the ash at the foot of the stone lies a small blue ribbon. Lira's. It is tied in a careful knot.

after_orochi_won.speaker: Kael
after_orochi_won.text: She left this for me. She is still alive. They both are.
* Kael folds the ribbon into his coat. With the serpent gone, the two roads above the fork lie open. Far off, a thin grey haze hangs over the Safaris.

after_orochi_won.speaker: Kael
after_orochi_won.text: I am coming. However far you take them.

norwoods_scorched_road.text: * The road is scorched in long black furrows, as if something huge and burning had been dragged along it, south toward the fork. The trail lantern at the fork is dark.
* In the soft earth at the edge of the burn, Kael finds two sets of small footprints. They walk close together. A little ahead of them, a man's long, even stride.

norwoods_scorched_road.speaker: Kael
norwoods_scorched_road.text: They were walking, not carried. He made them walk all this way.

norwoods_serpent_hollow.text: * The ground sinks into a great coiled hollow where Orochi slept. Above it, under a split tree, the remains of a camp. The fire was put out with ash, not water.
* Beside a single bedroll, two small blankets lie folded. Lira and Tobin slept here, or tried to.

norwoods_serpent_hollow.speaker: Kael
norwoods_serpent_hollow.text: He waited here while it woke. He wanted to watch it come for whoever followed.

norwoods_mangal_roots.text: * The Giant Mangal rises above the canopy, older than any tree Kael has seen. Its roots are as thick as houses.
* A notice from the Dundean hunters is nailed to the board: GIANT MANGAL CLOSED. BARBARIAN SIGHTED ON THE UPPER FLOORS. BY ORDER OF THE LODGE.
* The barricade at the root door has been pushed aside, just far enough for a man to pass. The edges of the planks are grey with ash, going in and coming out.

mangal_crossroads.text: * At the shrine, every candle is dark. The wicks are pinched flat. Someone put them out one by one.
* The crossroads sign has lost one of its arms. A fallen mangal trunk lies across the north road, and beyond it the earth has slid away into a ravine.

safaris_riverbank.text: * The small house by the river stands empty. On the jetty, pushed under a plank where someone walking ahead would not see it, lies a little carved wooden dragon.

safaris_riverbank.speaker: Kael
safaris_riverbank.text: Tobin's. I carved this for him last winter. He never lets it out of his hand.

safaris_riverbank.speaker: Kael
safaris_riverbank.text: He hid it. Not from me. From him.
* Kael puts it in his coat, beside the ribbon. The river runs on, quiet and cold.

dundean_square.text: * Dundean is quiet. Shutters are closed in daylight, and the hunters at the lodge door watch the road with their hands on their weapons.

dundean_square.speaker: Kael
dundean_square.text: Halvard said to ask here first. Someone must have seen them.

first.speaker: Old Edda
first.text: Dun ar, open road. Out of the Norwoods, on foot, at your age, with a guild hatchling at your heel. Sit down before you fall down.

first.speaker: Kael
first.text: I am looking for a man covered in grey ash. He has two children with him. A girl and a boy. My sister and brother.

first.speaker: Old Edda
first.text: ...Then you have had a worse road than any of us. Brann at the valley gate saw something, three mornings ago. Talk to him. He will not lie to you.

first.speaker: Old Edda
first.text: The lodge has barred the Giant Mangal stair and the east valley gate. Only the hunters can lift those bars, and they lift them when the lodge says. Not before.

first.speaker: Old Edda
first.text: There is a bed here if you need it. No questions, no coin. Whatever you are walking into, you will not do it well half asleep.

repeat: The grass hears. Keep your voice low on the roads, boy. The Safaris are not as empty as they look.
The hunters lift the barricades when they judge it safe. Not before. Arguing with the lodge has never moved a bar in this town.
Eat something. I have buried hunters braver than you who forgot to.
Forty years I have kept this house. Everyone who comes in off that road comes in hungry.
edda.name: Old Edda

first.speaker: Brann
first.text: Dun ar. Stay back from the gate. ...You have the look of someone chasing something.

first.speaker: Kael
first.text: A man in grey ash, with two children. Did he come through here?

first.speaker: Brann
first.text: At first light, three mornings ago, across the Safaris. Grey, like a burnt-out fire walking. A girl at his side, and a small boy who kept looking back.

first.speaker: Brann
first.text: He took the valley road east. At the top of the valley, a dragon keeps the pass to Longdale. The lodge barred this gate behind him.

first.speaker: Kael
first.text: The boy kept looking back. He was looking for me.

first.speaker: Brann
first.text: I had three hunters with me, and none of us moved. That gate stays shut until the lodge says otherwise. I am sorry.

repeat: The valley road runs east to the pass, and the dragon that keeps it. Longdale lies beyond. Nobody walks it alone.
He did not hurry. He walked like a man who knew nothing in the Safaris would try to stop him.
He never once looked behind him. The boy did that for both of them.
The bar comes up when the lodge says. I have kept this gate twenty years, and my father kept it before me.
brann.name: Brann

frontier_lines: The stair to the second floor is lashed shut with rope and timber. A lodge mark: BARBARIAN ALERT. NO PASSAGE ABOVE THE FIRST FLOOR.
Seven more floors rise above this one, and something up there has made the Dundean hunters afraid. The way up will have to wait until the lodge lifts the bar.
The north road to Ringfeld is buried under a fallen mangal trunk. Beyond it, the earth has slid into a ravine. No one is getting through this way.
Past the ravine, the road goes on toward Ringfeld and the sea. There must be another way round to the coast.
The valley gate is barred from the inside. Brann's mark is on the bar. The road beyond runs east, up the valley, toward the dragon that keeps the pass.
He took them this way. Kael presses his hand to the cold wood. Not yet. But soon.
map_text_addendum: Beyond the Waystone fork, two high roads climb out of the hollow. The left road crosses the scorched part of the Norwoods, past Serpent's Hollow where Orochi slept, to the roots of the Giant Mangal. The dungeon rises eight floors, but the Dundean lodge has barred it above the first. The right road winds into the Forest of Mangal, past an abandoned building site, to a crossroads whose north road to Ringfeld is blocked by a fallen trunk. The two roads meet again in the Safaris, open grassland cut by a river, with a small house on its bank. Dundean stands at the heart of the Safaris. From its valley gate, a road runs east up the South Earlsome valley to a pass the hunters say a dragon keeps, and beyond it to Longdale. The hunters lift the bars when they judge it safe. The map does not end here. It has only been drawn this far.
